svg.aria-label: Diagram: EC2 Image Builder now hosts the AWS DevOps Agent in its console as two separate features that share one agent space and one set of permissions. Troubleshoot analyses a failed image pipeline by reading failure context, build logs and Amazon CloudWatch logs, workflow step executions, networking and permissions, components and recipe configuration, network connectivity, and build history, then returns a root cause analysis and remediation steps, and it performs read-only analysis so resources are not modified. Create with AI drafts values for seven resource types, validates them with a dry run before showing them, and applies them to the console form, but the documentation states that you create or update the resource yourself and the AI does not create or modify resources. A dry run proves Image Builder would accept the configuration, not that the configuration is the one you intended. The one place a submission goes wider than it looks is suggested dependent resources, which are real resources in your account that can incur costs when you use them in builds, and which Image Builder creates when you create the parent resource. Both features need an agent space and the aidevops permissions ListAgentSpaces, CreateChat and SendChatMessage, plus CreateAgentSpace only if you want Image Builder to create the agent space rather than bringing your own. Billing is separate from Image Builder at 0.0083 dollars per agent-second, creating an agent space is free, there are no charges while the agent is idle, and other services the agent queries on your behalf such as Amazon CloudWatch Logs bill those queries at their standard rates.
svg.title: The agent drafts and validates; a human submits the form
svg.text: Two features in one drawer. Neither of them changes a resource.
“You create or update the resource yourself. The AI doesn’t create or modify resources.”
TROUBLESHOOT — A READER
Failure context · build + CloudWatch logs · workflow steps
networking · recipe · connectivity · build history
“read-only analysis. Your resources are not modified.”
A wrong answer costs an afternoon.
CREATE WITH AI — A DRAFTER
Components · recipes · container recipes · pipelines
workflows · infrastructure config · distribution settings
Values land in the form. You press the button.
A wrong answer becomes configuration.
What “verifies the configuration” means
“Validates the values with a dry run before it shows them, and fixes values that Image Builder rejects.”
A dry run answers ‘would Image Builder accept this?’ — never ‘is this the image you meant?’
And if validation fails you are told, not blocked: apply to form anyway, and fix the fields yourself.
The one click that goes wider than it looks
“Suggested dependent resources are real resources in your account. They can incur costs when you use
them in builds.” And Image Builder creates them when you create the parent — where your eye already is.
FOUR PERMISSIONS, ONE OPTIONAL
ListAgentSpaces CreateChat SendChatMessage
CreateAgentSpace — omit if you bring your own
Creating needs your own Image Builder permissions too.
TWO BILLS, NEITHER IN THE ANNOUNCEMENT
The agent: “$0.0083 per agent-second”, nothing when idle.
The services it queries for you: “standard rates”.
Wide investigations read a lot of log data on your account.
Also: the agent space Region is where your requests are processed, even when the resources stay in yours;
follow-ups cap at 4,000 characters; copying the report does not copy the follow-up answers.
One feature reads and cannot act. The other writes a draft and still cannot act. The signature stays yours.
